title: Elastic burst credit system and overage protections for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Customers with Dedicated capacity sometimes need short-lived throughput spikes (eg. marketing launches, black-friday style pulses, model warm-ups) that exceed committed throughput. Current options (surge pools + immediate overage billing) cause either hard throttles or surprising invoices. Goal: introduce an elastic burst credit system that allows short bursts without immediate overage charges, ties into existing surge pool mechanics, and provides clear invoice behavior and tenant controls. Scope: 1) Credit accrual model (burst credits earned based on unused committed throughput over time). 2) Mechanism to consume credits during bursts before hitting surge pool/overage. 3) Admin controls for fleets (max burst multiplier, credit caps, automatic refill policies). 4) Billing signals & invoice line items to reflect credit consumption vs. overage. 5) Metrics, alerts and console UI surfaces for credits. Non-goals: changing baseline reserved pricing or SLA guarantees; designing new surge pool autoscaler (we integrate with existing pool controller). Proposed approach: - Add a credit-tracking table per-fleet (credit_balance, last_accrual_ts, accrual_rate_config) persisted in fleet state store. - Accrual policy: fractional of unused committed tokens per minute, configurable per-tier; default accrual equals 10% of unused capacity per hour (configurable). - Consumption policy: incoming requests that would exceed committed throughput first deduct from credit_balance up to a per-request cap; if exhausted, fall back to surge pool; if surge pool unavailable, enforce configured throttle or apply overage billing. - Fleet controls: new fleet config fields (max_burst_multiplier, credit_cap, accrual_enabled). - Billing: record credit_consumed and overage_tokens in billing events; credit consumption reduces billed overage at defined discount (credits represent pre-authorized buffer). - UX: Console shows credit balance, projected time-to-refill, and controls to enable/disable accrual. - Monitoring: SLI/SLO changes to account for credit-backed bursts; new dashboards and alerts when credit balance < 10% or accrual stalled. Acceptance criteria and rollout in separate section below.
acceptance_criteria: Credit accrual backend persists per-fleet balances and accrues at configured rate in canary cluster
Incoming requests that exceed committed throughput consume credit_balance before surge pool or overage in integration tests
Console UI surfaces fleet credit balance and allows toggling accrual and max_burst_multiplier
Billing pipeline emits credit_consumed events and invoices subtract credit usage from immediate overage charges (e2e billing test)
Metrics: credit_balance_gauge, credit_accrual_rate, credit_consumption_counter available in Prometheus and used in alerting
Feature gated behind fleet config flag and rollout follows canary -> partial roll -> global pattern with automatic rollback on errors
